geo.label: March lift-off priced, pace contested
parts: Macro Stance

The US is in a tightening cycle that has not formally started but is already working through the front end. January consumer prices rose 7.5% on an annual basis, the highest since 1982, CNBC reported [[n2116]]. Reuters read the January FOMC minutes as showing a Fed not wed to a particular pace of rate hikes [[n2224]], while Al Jazeera stressed that officials are prepared to move faster if inflation persists [[n1369]]. That keeps a March move as the base case and leaves the size of the step as the market's live variable. Growth is not yet the constraint, with industrial production rebounding according to The Real Economy Blog [[n2155]]; confidence is the weak link, and Yahoo Finance described consumers as being in a deep funk [[n2131]].
Rates & Curve

The 2Y closed at 1.52% and the 10Y at 2.03%, a 10Y-2Y spread of +51 bps on a positively sloped curve (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-16). Over 20 observations the 2Y is +48 bps from 1.04% and the 10Y +20 bps from 1.83%, so the spread has narrowed by 28 bps: a bear flattening, with both yields up and the 2Y up more. Over the last five observations the 2Y added +16 bps against +9 bps for the 10Y. Reuters said the curve is pricing Fed tightening and showing fears of a policy error [[n2218]], and Bloomberg warned that Treasury market liquidity is eroding with the Fed's course a gamble [[n2215]]. Thin liquidity plus a fast-repricing front end keeps equity volatility high: the VIX closed at 24.29 index points, -1.41 points on the session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16).
New / Most Important

The minutes neither validated the half-point camp nor shut it out. Reuters had the Fed raising rates 25 bps in March, with calls for 50 bps growing louder [[n1360]]. Equities absorbed the readout calmly: the S&P 500 closed at 4,475.01 index points, +0.09% on the session but -2.45% over five sessions, the Nasdaq 100 slipped -0.12% to 14,603.64 index points and the DXY eased -0.30% to 95.70 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). Politico adds a smaller wrinkle, reporting Republicans delaying the vote on Biden's Fed nominees and turning up the heat on Sarah Bloom Raskin [[n2214]].
Playbook ✓

Action: stay underweight long-duration growth and keep portfolio duration short, expressing the rate view at the front end rather than through the 10Y. Trigger: a hawkish data surprise that lifts the 2Y further above 1.52% while the 10Y lags would extend the bear flattening and favour energy and banks over software. What changes the call: a VIX back below its 23.85 level of 20 sessions ago together with a 10Y-2Y spread that stops compressing from +51 bps would signal the March step is fully priced and justify rebuilding quality growth (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16; US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-16). A Ukraine escalation would rally Treasuries but widen credit spreads, so it is a hedge, not an entry point.

geo.label: Gradual ECB, gas-hostage growth
parts: Macro Stance

Europe sits between an ECB that wants to move slowly and an energy shock it cannot control. Reuters reported Lagarde repeating her pledge for a gradual policy shift [[n1291]], and Bloomberg quoted her saying the ECB will act at the right time but only gradually [[n1298]]. Reuters has the deposit rate rising to -0.25% by year-end [[n1290]], a slow path next to UK inflation climbing to 5.5%, the highest since 1992 [[n1336]].
Activity & Inflation

Activity is reopening rather than rolling over: DW reported Germany planning an end to Covid restrictions [[n1325]]. Prices are the problem. Eurostat flagged energy prices on the rise in the euro area in 2021 [[n2114]], and Dutch TTF gas closed at 69.79 EUR/MWh even after a -6.21% five-session drop (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). The BBC reported UK wage growth lagging the rising cost of living [[n1316]], the template for the euro area's real-income squeeze: inflation erodes spending power before it lifts pay.
New / Most Important

Putin told Scholz that Russia does not want war in Europe, DW reported [[n1302]], and Reuters quoted him saying Nord Stream 2 would cement Europe's energy security [[n1312]]: reassurance that doubles as leverage. Markets are only half convinced. The Stoxx 600 closed at 467.77 index points, +0.04% on the session and -2.73% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16), and STOXX noted increased VSTOXX futures activity amid the pullback and ahead of the French elections [[n1338]].
Playbook ✓

Action: stay neutral on broad European equities, favouring energy majors and autos with pricing power over the banks that sold off hardest; Societe Generale is -4.87% and Raiffeisen Bank International -7.16% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). Trigger: TTF back above its 75.60 EUR/MWh level of 20 sessions ago would signal the gas premium returning. What changes the call: an ECB moving faster than the -0.25% year-end path [[n1290]] would favour banks over autos.

geo.label: Easing into a property drag
parts: Macro Stance

China is the one major economy where policy is moving the other way. Al Jazeera reported the central bank chief vowing support amid weak links in the economy [[n0261]], and Reuters reported slowing inflation leaving room for policy easing [[n0245]]. Bloomberg's January framing still holds: as the Fed hikes, China's central bank is seizing the moment for stimulus [[n0162]]. The stance is Bullish on the policy impulse, not on the cycle. The growth base is soft, property is still deleveraging and Hong Kong's Omicron wave is testing the zero-Covid model at an awkward moment.
PMIs & Activity

The latest activity data argue for support rather than celebration. Reuters reported January factory activity contracting as Covid lockdowns bit, according to the Caixin PMI [[n0167]]. That followed 8.1% GDP growth in 2021, the fastest in ten years, per Global Times [[n0151]], and fixed-asset investment up 4.9% for the year, per Macau Business [[n0153]]. The annual figure flatters the run-rate, because the strength was front-loaded and investment growth was already modest. Services face a fresh hit from Hong Kong, where the BBC described hospitals as overwhelmed amid a spike in cases [[n0264]] and Al Jazeera reported Xi telling the city to control the outbreak [[n0276]]. With the mainland sticking to its strategy, any consumption rebound stays capped.
Credit Impulse

Credit is where the turn is visible. Reuters reported Chinese government bond yields rising on faster January credit growth [[n0180]], a sign the bond market reads the lending surge as real. Bloomberg reported the PBOC pumping in more liquidity and spurring gains in Chinese stocks [[n0238]], after CNBC reported January cuts to key lending rates, including one for the first time in nearly two years [[n0157]]. The mechanism matters: lower rates cut the cost of rolling local-government and developer debt, and a stronger credit impulse tends to lead industrial activity by several quarters. The limit is discipline, with the South China Morning Post reporting Beijing telling banks to support rural infrastructure without adding to hidden debt [[n0227]].
Property

Property is the drag policy is cushioning rather than reflating. Reuters reported China giving property firms easier access to escrow funds [[n0179]], and the Khmer Times reported affordable rental housing being excluded from property credit controls [[n0259]]: targeted relief, not a blanket reversal of deleveraging. Stress is still moving through the developer chain. Bloomberg, citing Caixin, reported China's Cedar unable to pay $3.1 billion overdue [[n0228]], and the South China Morning Post reported Evergrande's chief executive dumping all his dollar bonds before the default [[n0187]]. Evergrande's vow to finish half of its units under construction this year, per Caixin Global [[n0188]], helps households but offers bondholders little. Business Recorder reported December new-home prices falling less on promotions and easing curbs [[n0148]], the first hint that support is reaching buyers.
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

Trade is turning from tailwind to friction. The BBC reported Washington accusing China of serious harm to workers through its trade practices [[n0274]], and the Peterson Institute found China bought none of the extra $200 billion of US exports promised in the Trump-era deal [[n0173]], a record that gives the administration reason to keep tariffs in place. Beijing is also using trade as a weapon, suspending Lithuanian beef, dairy and beer imports as the Taiwan row grew, Reuters reported [[n0182]], while India banned 54 Chinese apps on security grounds, per the South China Morning Post [[n0233]]. On Russia, the South China Morning Post quoted Beijing saying Western sanctions would worsen the Ukraine crisis [[n1483]], a reminder that a sanctions escalation could put Chinese banks and exporters in the crossfire.
Markets & Flows

Offshore equities are responding to the policy divergence faster than onshore. The Hang Seng closed at 24,718.90 index points, +1.49% on the session and +1.38% over 20 sessions, while the Shanghai Composite closed at 3,465.83 index points, +0.57% on the day but -3.66% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). Tencent is +3.64% over 20 sessions at 452.28 HKD, and Alibaba's Hong Kong line rose +3.46% on the session to 122.50 HKD. CNBC reported banks from Credit Suisse to Goldman Sachs saying it is time to buy Chinese stocks [[n0247]], but flows are selective: Caixin Global reported Hillhouse buying electric-vehicle makers while ditching Alibaba and Bilibili [[n0754]]. The currency is the release valve, with Reuters reporting the yuan slipping as divergent China-U.S. monetary policy exerts downward pressure [[n0254]].
New / Most Important

The new element is the explicit pledge of support from the central bank chief [[n0261]] arriving alongside softer inflation; together they make a further cut in policy rates or reserve requirements the path of least resistance. The second is Hong Kong, where the WSJ reported hospital wards overflowing as Omicron defies zero-Covid policies [[n0248]], a direct hit to the city's consumption and to confidence in the strategy. The third is Washington's trade report: PBS carried the US charge that China's aggressive trade policies cause serious harm [[n0273]], which raises the odds that tariffs stay.
Playbook ✓

Action: overweight offshore China internet against onshore A-shares, using KWEB, +2.91% over 20 sessions at 37.88 USD, against ASHR, -2.78% over 20 sessions at 36.71 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). Trigger: a cut in policy rates or reserve ratios, or another month of faster credit growth, confirms the easing impulse. What changes the call: a developer default large enough to hit bank capital, or a Hong Kong outbreak forcing mainland restrictions. ⚠ Divergence: easing is being delivered into a contracting factory PMI and a property sector still unable to pay its bills, so the policy signal points up while the activity and credit-quality signals still point down.

geo.label: Ultra-easy BOJ, chip-constrained output
parts: Macro Stance

Japan has a clean demand rebound and the least policy pressure among the majors. Reuters reported the economy rebounding on solid spending, with Omicron clouding the outlook [[n1548]]. The BOJ remains the most dovish major central bank, yet Reuters also flagged that a board reshuffle may open scope for a less dovish BOJ [[n1556]]. That is a slow-burning option rather than a near-term event, but it matters globally: any hint of normalisation in Tokyo would remove one of the anchors holding down long-end yields everywhere. The Nikkei 225 closed at 27,460.40 index points, +2.22% on the session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16).
Activity & Currency

Manufacturing is gated by chips, not demand. Automotive Logistics reported Toyota cutting March production plans because of the chip shortage [[n1973]], and CNET reported the shortage hurting Toyota more than Nissan [[n1957]]. Toyota closed at 2,192.50 JPY, -4.51% over five sessions, while chip-equipment makers rallied, Tokyo Electron +4.91% to 57,930.00 JPY and Advantest +4.78% to 9,650.00 JPY on the session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). Supply is responding: the Asahi Shimbun reported TSMC expanding its new Japan chip factory with Denso taking a stake [[n1559]]. On the currency, the mechanism is the rate gap: with the US 10Y at 2.03% and the BOJ pinning domestic yields, a wider spread tends to weaken the yen, flattering exporters' earnings while raising the bill for imported energy (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-16).
Playbook ✓

Action: prefer Japanese semiconductor equipment over autos until chip supply normalises. Trigger: Toyota restoring its production plans, or the board change turning into explicit BOJ guidance, would broaden the rally. What changes the call: an Omicron-driven consumption relapse that undoes the rebound, or a risk-off move that hits high-beta chip names first; Tokyo Electron is still -11.64% over 20 sessions and Sony Group -13.32% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). Japan remains the cheapest hedge against a global duration shock only while the BOJ stays put.

geo.label: QE over, RBA testing patience
parts: Macro Stance

Australia is a test of RBA patience. The Sydney Morning Herald reported the end of QE with a murky future for $650b of assets [[n0023]], and Governor Lowe's February policy statement remains the baseline [[n0016]]. The AFR argued inflation will force an RBA rate pivot [[n0010]] after a shock spike to 3.5 per cent [[n0009]], and Bloomberg had already described a bond meltdown haunting the central bank as inflation builds [[n0005]]. The bank's credibility now rests on how quickly it concedes that the labour market has tightened faster than its own forecasts assumed.
Demand & Financing

Demand is firm but cost-pressured. The Australian reported the jobless rate at a 13-year low as an RBA hike loomed [[n0004]], and the AFR warned that rising rents could be the sleeper factor for inflation [[n0030]]. Company results were uneven: Reuters reported Wesfarmers' profit dipping after the pandemic storm [[n0898]], while ABC reported CSL posting weaker profit [[n0056]], yet CSL jumped +8.51% on the session to 263.69 AUD and the S&P/ASX 200 closed at 7,284.90 index points, +1.08% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). The next labour-force print is the decisive input for how long the RBA can wait.
Playbook ✓

Action: favour the major banks over consumer discretionary. The Australian reported Commonwealth Bank's Mike Vacy Lyle saying bullish banks see a brighter outlook [[n0533]], and lenders tend to gain once hikes arrive. Trigger: another strong jobs report pulls hike expectations forward. What changes the call: weak wage growth that lets the RBA stay patient, or an iron-ore setback; BHP is -2.05% over five sessions at 42.14 AUD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16).

geo.label: Hiking into 9% inflation
parts: Macro Stance

Poland is running its hottest inflation of the century into the sharpest security risk on its border. GUS put January inflation at 9.2%, Forsal.pl reported [[n1769]], and Bankier.pl noted that inflation had passed 9% [[n1772]]. The Monetary Policy Council answered with another hike, taking rates to their highest in almost nine years, Rzeczpospolita reported [[n1635]], and the individual investors' association SII argued the NBP has not yet said its last word [[n1636]]. The labour market gives the RPP room: registered unemployment was 5.6% in January, according to the labour ministry figure carried by RadioMaryja.pl [[n1632]], and average pay rose 9.6% in 2021, per pb.pl [[n1638]]. The stance is Mixed because nominal growth and bank margins are strong while real incomes, the currency and the fiscal mix are all exposed to the same geopolitical shock.
Markets

The zloty is the shock absorber. Bankier.pl reported it at its strongest in eight months on February 10 [[n1653]], then recovering losses on February 14 as the Ukraine question hit markets [[n1751]]. Equities are cheaper but not calm: the iShares MSCI Poland ETF closed at 21.37 USD, +0.61% on the session and -2.64% over 20 sessions, and the WIG20 total-return tracker at 38.16 PLN is -4.46% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). Parkiet asked how markets would react if a global armed conflict broke out [[n1804]], and Bankier.pl asked whether this is still a correction or already a bear market [[n1645]]. Rates are reshaping household balance sheets: INNPoland.pl said deposits paying 3-4% are possible but with a catch [[n1755]], and Obserwator Gospodarczy asked why deposit rates are not rising [[n1766]]. That lag is exactly why Parkiet sees room for listed banks to extend their bull run [[n1659]].
Fiscal & Politics

Fiscal policy is looser than the deficit suggests. Bankier.pl reported the finance ministry's estimate of the 2021 state budget deficit at 26.3 billion zlotys [[n1683]], and Rzeczpospolita argued that inflation helps the government cope with its debt [[n1634]]. The Polski Ład tax reform is the political cost centre: PolsatNews.pl reported a deputy finance minister dismissed over its problems [[n1679]], Interia ran a poll on whether it damaged Law and Justice [[n1741]], and Next Gazeta.pl reported that President Duda, who signed it, now wants comprehensive changes [[n1792]]. 300Gospodarka.pl reported pension indexation will cost more than the budget assumed because of the higher index [[n1694]]. Brussels has also gained leverage: Reuters reported the EU's top court throwing out the Polish and Hungarian challenge to the money-for-democracy mechanism [[n1609]], EUobserver said the ruling clears funding cuts for rule-breaking states [[n1608]], and Rzeczpospolita reported Justice Minister Ziobro attacking Prime Minister Morawiecki after it [[n1814]].
Corporate & Sectors

Energy security has become corporate strategy. eKoszalin reported KGHM targeting small modular reactors in Poland by 2029 [[n1776]], Biznes Wprost quoted Jacek Sasin on his way to Washington with good news for Poland [[n1720]], and POWER Magazine reported Poland securing a NuScale SMR [[n1591]]. KGHM closed at 154.30 PLN, +5.94% over five sessions, and coking-coal miner JSW is +14.77% over 20 sessions at 47.01 PLN (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). Gas is the vulnerability: the energy regulator URE reported a record price for gas imported from EU countries in the last quarter of 2021 [[n1743]], and wnp.pl reported legal changes alarming gas customers before PSG moved to reassure them [[n1816]]. In consumer names, CD Projekt released the next-generation Cyberpunk 2077 update with a free trial [[n1757]], but Antyweb reported the director of The Witcher 3 leaving to found Rebel Wolves [[n1811]]. DlaHandlu.pl reported nearly 2,300 hires planned by Aldi, Biedronka, Dino and Lidl [[n1809]], a wage-cost signal for Dino, which is -14.45% over 20 sessions at 293.00 PLN.
Geopolitics & Security

Poland is NATO's logistics hub for the crisis. Reuters reported the US sending 3,000 additional troops to Poland [[n1580]], CNBC said US troops there are preparing to help refugees if Russia invades Ukraine [[n1586]], and Notes From Poland reported a US welcome centre opening for citizens fleeing Ukraine [[n1610]]. Diplomacy is not producing relief: after meeting Lavrov in Moscow, Foreign Minister Rau said European security is in a deep crisis, TVN24 reported [[n1785]]. The Atlantic Council warned an invasion could come with less than 12 hours' notice [[n1606]], and NATO defence ministers issued a statement on the situation in and around Ukraine [[n1607]]. For markets, the shock would travel through the zloty's risk premium, through gas, given that IntelliNews describes Central Europe as still tied to Russia's pipeline network [[n1596]], and through the fiscal cost of any refugee inflow.
New / Most Important

Three developments matter most. First, 9.2% inflation [[n1769]] keeps the RPP hiking, which supports bank earnings but squeezes consumer stocks: Allegro fell -3.82% on the session and is -14.61% over 20 sessions at 34.33 PLN, and LPP is -9.49% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). Second, the BBC reported Poland and Hungary losing the EU funding fight over laws [[n1601]], which hardens the standoff over EU money. Third, the security premium rises and falls with Moscow's signals, which is why the zloty's recovery [[n1751]] remains fragile. Put together, the domestic data argue for higher rates and a stronger currency, while the border argues for a risk premium, and investors are being paid to hold that tension only in the banks.
Playbook ✓

Action: overweight Polish banks against consumer discretionary, holding PKO Bank Polski at 47.21 PLN and Bank Pekao at 135.25 PLN, up +2.04% on the session, against Allegro and LPP (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). Trigger: another RPP hike or an upside core-inflation surprise extends the margin story. What changes the call: an invasion that sends the zloty sharply weaker and forces emergency action from the NBP would hit banks through risk premia, while an EU funds compromise would favour domestic cyclicals instead. ⚠ Divergence: rate hikes and a tight labour market argue for bank earnings upside, yet PKO Bank Polski is -3.65% over five sessions while KGHM and JSW rally, so the market is pricing security risk and commodity scarcity ahead of the domestic rate story.
Narrative

Technology is being repriced by the front end of the curve more than by its own earnings. XLK closed at 158.75 USD, -0.10% on the session and -3.24% over five sessions, with Microsoft at 299.50 USD and Apple at 172.55 USD both lower on the day (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). Dispersion is extreme: Adobe is -8.44% over five sessions while Datadog is +32.85% over 20 sessions.
Reported

Reuters reported Cisco raising its annual earnings forecast and announcing $15 billion in share buybacks [[n1181]], and CNBC's Investing Club said Cisco defied the doubters with a beat and raise [[n1193]].
EPS Upside Watch

Networking has pricing power while supply is tight, and Cisco's raise is the template. CRN reported IDC data showing Lenovo topping HP and Dell in the best year for PC shipments in a decade [[n0732]], a demanding base for devices, so upside sits in enterprise infrastructure.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The consensus treats all software as a duration trade to avoid; the better split is profitability. The WSJ reported Microsoft keeping its finance head count flat with AI, bots and other tech [[n1073]], the kind of operating leverage the market will still pay for with the 10Y at 2.03% (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-16).
Narrative

Communication services is where the pandemic hangover meets an advertising reset. XLC closed at 69.80 USD, -7.55% over 20 sessions; Meta Platforms (FB) is -32.24% over 20 sessions at 216.54 USD and Netflix -22.83% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16).
Reported

EPS Upside Watch

Scale still earns a premium: TechCrunch reported Disney+ outshining Netflix with 11.8M new subscribers and a strong forecast [[n1062]], and Walt Disney is +6.19% over five sessions at 156.35 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). Mashable reported Snapchat testing ads in Snap Stories and sharing the revenue with creators [[n0774]], a modest monetisation lever.

Meta's slide has turned it into a value debate, but the legal tail is lengthening: Reuters reported a $90 million privacy settlement over user tracking [[n0738]], and Al Jazeera reported Texas suing over facial recognition [[n0638]]. Cheap is not the same as de-risked.

Financials gain from the bear flattening only at the front end. XLF closed at 40.23 USD, +2.50% over 20 sessions, with JPMorgan Chase +4.08% over 20 sessions at 155.00 USD, but Morgan Stanley is -6.97% over five sessions and Upstart swung +35.65% in a single session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16).
Reported

Regional banks, with KRE +0.97% over five sessions at 75.72 USD, are the cleaner expression than capital-markets houses (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16).
⚡ Breaking Convention

The near-term risk is legal, not credit. Reuters reported Morgan Stanley's role in the Archegos collapse speeding up block-trade probes [[n0886]], and the WSJ reported regulators probing block trading at Morgan Stanley, Goldman and other firms [[n0599]]. City AM reported Berkshire Hathaway dumping Visa and Mastercard and buying $1bn of Nubank [[n0935]], a vote for challenger fintech over incumbent networks.
Narrative

Energy is the market's cleanest hedge against inflation and geopolitics at once. Reuters reported oil hitting 7-year highs as the market feared a Russian attack on Ukraine [[n0120]]. Brent closed at 94.81 USD/bbl, +7.20% over 20 sessions, and WTI at 93.66 USD/bbl (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16).
Reported

Reuters said the IEA's demand revision confirmed a tighter oil market [[n0641]], and The Intercept reported Saudi Arabia rejecting Biden's plea to increase production [[n1990]]. XLE closed at 68.58 USD, +6.66% over 20 sessions, with Schlumberger +12.37% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16).
EPS Upside Watch

The upside is in services and gas: Schlumberger rose +3.99% on the session to 41.69 USD and Henry Hub gas jumped +9.54% to 4.72 USD/MMBtu (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). CNBC reported Warren Buffett increasing an energy bet by more than a third [[n0604]], and Bloomberg argued oil's Covid crash set the world up for $100 crude [[n0141]] by starving investment.

Industrials are split between an aerospace recovery, defence demand and freight inflation. XLI closed at 101.01 USD, +0.53% on the session but -2.37% over 20 sessions; ITA closed at 106.97 USD and Northrop Grumman rose +2.31% to 393.66 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16).

EPS Upside Watch

Pricing power is the swing factor. Supply Chain Dive reported Starbucks accelerating price increases to offset Omicron-related costs [[n1139]], CBS News reported Chipotle planning to raise menu prices again [[n1092]], and Barron's reported Marriott stock rising as the chain rebounds from the pandemic [[n1164]].

Forbes reported Kellogg joining Chipotle and Starbucks in planning price hikes this year due to inflation [[n1070]]. The upside sits with brands that can price without losing volume; Procter & Gamble rose +0.76% on the session to 158.01 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16).

Walmart's next print is the real test of the mass-market consumer: if the cost pressure visible in Mexico shows up in US margins, staples stop working as a hedge. Reuters reported inflation turning up the heat on Unilever even as it backs down on M&A [[n0326]]; scale is not immunity.

Health care is losing its pandemic premium while keeping its defensive role. XLV closed at 130.57 USD, -2.69% over five sessions; Moderna is -12.79% over 20 sessions at 151.81 USD, while AbbVie is +7.88% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16).

Moderna's chief executive told CNBC it is reasonable to think the pandemic may be in its final stages [[n0880]], and Reuters reported Moderna eyeing a booster by August, with no clarity yet on whether it must be Omicron-specific [[n0882]].
EPS Upside Watch

Covid revenue is now a downside risk to estimates, so upside sits in durable franchises and launches. Fierce Pharma reported AbbVie's Qulipta gaining ground with doctors for migraine prevention as the company pressures Biohaven's Nurtec [[n0287]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

Early-stage biotech is where value is appearing: STAT reported some newly public biotech companies trading below cash [[n1877]]. With XBI +1.23% over 20 sessions at 94.65 USD, small biotech may be nearer a floor than the large-cap Covid winners (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16).
Narrative

Materials are the supply-shock beneficiaries. XLB closed at 85.46 USD, +0.73% on the session; aluminium is +9.27% over 20 sessions at 3,320.00 USD/t and Alcoa +30.54% at 77.84 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16).
Reported

Reuters reported Glencore posting record earnings while setting aside $1.5 billion for probes [[n1154]], and BHP's first-half profit beating estimates and triggering talk of M&A [[n0567]]. Barrick declared an increased dividend and a performance dividend policy [[n0830]], while Mining Weekly reported Vale producing less iron than expected [[n0041]], a supply signal for bulk prices.
EPS Upside Watch

Reuters columnist Andy Home argued that an LME stocks surge failed to cool a red-hot aluminium market [[n0177]]; high energy costs tend to keep marginal smelters offline, which supports prices for producers still running. Fertilisers are a second leg, with CF Industries +3.05% on the session and +11.24% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16).
⚡ Breaking Convention

Gold miners are outrunning the metal: GDX is +6.14% over five sessions against +1.90% for gold at 1,871.50 USD/oz (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). That operating leverage is a cheaper inflation hedge than bullion if real yields stall.
Narrative

Listed real estate is paying for higher yields while private capital pays up for assets. XLRE closed at 45.27 USD, -4.49% over five sessions, as the 10Y rose +9 bps over five observations (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16; US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-16).
Reported

The Real Deal reported Blackstone buying a multifamily REIT in a $5.8B deal [[n0834]], and Bloomberg reported Wynn Resorts selling its Boston property to Realty Income for $1.7 billion [[n0813]]. Both deals show buyers with long-dated capital still willing to pay for real assets as public valuations fall.
EPS Upside Watch

Rental housing is the growth engine. The Washington Post reported investors buying a record share of homes in 2021 [[n2157]], and the San Francisco Fed asked whether rising rents will push up future inflation [[n2143]]. Rent resets lift REIT cash flows with a lag.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The private-public gap is the real trade: when Blackstone pays up for listed REITs, discounts tend to close through takeovers rather than through falling yields. But the Orange County Register reported mortgage rates surging to a two-year high, with the 30-year at 3.69% [[n2119]], which caps housing-linked names.
Narrative

Utilities have lost their bond-proxy shelter. XLU closed at 66.30 USD, -3.54% over five sessions; NextEra is -8.91% over 20 sessions at 75.23 USD, Duke Energy -4.97% and Southern Company -4.72% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). The sector is trading as a bond, and the bond is losing.
Reported

Utility Dive reported Duke Energy, on track to eliminate coal by 2035, expanding its net zero carbon goal to include indirect emissions [[n0621]], and E&E News reported its plan to exit all coal and double renewables [[n0427]].
EPS Upside Watch

The rate base grows with the energy transition, but fuel costs bite first: Henry Hub gas rose +9.54% on the session and +17.66% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). Forbes reported France vowing to build more nuclear after high gas prices [[n1986]], a sign that regulated investment is political rather than optional.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The usual contrarian argument is that a Ukraine shock would pull yields down and rescue the sector, but the same shock would lift gas costs, which makes utilities a poor hedge this time. Prefer nuclear-heavy generators to gas-exposed ones.
Narrative

European autos are the region's clearest pricing-power story. The STOXX autos tracker closed at 62.27 EUR, -4.30% over 20 sessions, but Mercedes-Benz Group is +7.49% over five sessions at 75.82 EUR and Renault +9.53% over 20 sessions, while Volkswagen preference shares slipped -1.16% on the session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). Dispersion rewards margin over volume.
Reported

Reuters reported Mercedes-Benz beating its profit forecast while seeing supply-chain headwinds in 2022 [[n0449]], and Bloomberg said Mercedes cars are more profitable than ever amid the chip shortage [[n1098]]. Reuters reported BMW paying $4.2 billion to take control of its Chinese joint venture [[n0415]].
EPS Upside Watch

Volume is the upside. Reuters reported Volkswagen expecting the chip shortage to ease later in 2022 [[n0933]], and the Mercedes-Benz CFO sees supply-chain woes easing in the second half [[n0448]]. Scarcity margins plus recovering volume is the earnings set-up.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Obserwator Gospodarczy reported German car production still about 40% below its level of three years ago [[n1668]]. That is the size of the recovery runway, provided a Russian invasion does not, as Fortune warned, make the chip shortage even worse [[n1971]].
Narrative

Semiconductors are splitting between data-centre and memory strength and weaker handset and PC exposure. SOXX closed at 490.25 USD, -2.85% over five sessions; AMD is -11.41% over five sessions while Micron is +9.01% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16).
Reported

Nvidia announced its fourth-quarter and fiscal 2022 results [[n0140]] and forecast upbeat current-quarter revenue, Al Jazeera reported [[n2006]]. Intel agreed to acquire Tower Semiconductor for $5.4 billion [[n0728]], and Tom's Hardware reported AMD's market cap surpassing Intel's for the first time [[n0657]].
EPS Upside Watch

Asia is leading: Tokyo Electron rose +4.91% and SK Hynix +2.76% on the session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16), and the Asahi Shimbun reported TSMC expanding its Japan chip factory [[n1559]]. Equipment orders follow foundry capex, so TSMC's ADR at 123.60 USD and ASML at 663.86 USD are the bellwethers to watch.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The underpriced risk is intellectual property and geopolitics. The South China Morning Post reported ASML flagging possible IP infringement by a Chinese little giant [[n0174]], and Reuters reported Taiwan boosting protection for its semiconductor secrets with an eye on China [[n0915]].

earnings_pattern.title: Reopening beats and cash returns rewarded; pandemic fades punished
parts: Rewarded

The market is paying for two things: a clean reopening story and cash returned to shareholders. Al Jazeera reported Airbnb seeing strong first-quarter revenue on a travel resurgence [[n0661]], and the stock rose +3.65% on the session and +10.09% over five sessions to 186.64 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). Cisco paired a beat and raise with buybacks [[n1193]], Mercedes-Benz beat its profit forecast [[n0449]] on scarcity pricing, and AIG's profit beat rested on general insurance strength [[n1179]]. Each combined pricing power with discipline on capital.
Punished

Results confirming a fading pandemic boost are being punished hard. Bloomberg said Roblox's worst post-earnings drop wrecks the stock-pop narrative [[n0143]], and it closed -26.51% at 53.87 USD; Al Jazeera reported Shopify plunging on a weaker growth outlook [[n2015]], closing -16.04% at 746.85 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). Reuters reported Paramount shares slumping as investments to beef up streaming spooked investors [[n0894]], and The Boston Globe tied Roblox's and Shopify's sales to the Covid decline [[n1200]]. Europe shows the same reflex: CNBC reported Delivery Hero's chief executive apologising to investors after a 30% stock plunge [[n0426]].
Pattern

The common thread is the second derivative of the pandemic. Where demand was pulled forward, in gaming hours, online-store formation and home fitness, the market extrapolates the fade; where demand was deferred, in travel, drinks away from home and premium cars, it extrapolates the catch-up. Guidance matters more than the quarter. DoorDash is the instructive exception, a pandemic winner whose revenue beat sent shares soaring 24% as, in Reuters' words, the food-delivery boom continues [[n0847]].
Attention into EPS

Attention now shifts to whether data-centre demand can offset consumer fatigue. Barron's framed Nvidia's report as the second act of a big day for the metaverse after Roblox [[n0862]], and the stock closed +0.06% at 265.11 USD before results, with Cisco at 54.25 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). Walmart's next print will set the tone for staples.
Playbook

Action: buy reopening beats that come with raised guidance and sell pandemic-era beneficiaries into strength until their outlooks stabilise. Trigger: a stock that holds its post-earnings gap through five sessions confirms the signal. What changes the call: if yields stop rising, the market will again pay for long-dated growth and the penalty for soft guidance will shrink.

underowned.title: Fertiliser and farm inputs: the food-inflation hedge
parts: Attention Gap

Fertiliser producers sit outside the energy and metals debate, yet MarketWatch argued the Russia-Ukraine crisis may make food-price inflation even worse [[n1996]]. Soybeans are +14.11% over 20 sessions at 1,587.50 US cents/bu (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16).
Exposure & Risk

CF Industries at 74.42 USD, Mosaic at 46.29 USD and Nutrien at 75.06 USD give direct exposure to nitrogen and potash pricing (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). The risk is that high gas costs squeeze nitrogen margins, or that a South American crop recovery deflates grain, with Successful Farming reporting a dry soybean crop looking to improve with rain [[n1999]].
Trigger to Watch

Grain holding its gains after a de-escalation headline would show the move is supply-driven rather than a war premium. Successful Farming reported soybean prices closing 36¢ per bushel higher on Wednesday [[n2017]].

underowned.title: Aluminium: an energy squeeze on supply
parts: Attention Gap

Aluminium has moved with far less attention than oil: the COMEX contract is +9.27% over 20 sessions at 3,320.00 USD/t, and Alcoa is +30.54% over the same span at 77.84 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16).
Exposure & Risk

Asia Financial described how a Chinese city became a global aluminium hub [[n0189]], a reminder that Chinese output policy sets the marginal tonne. The risks are a fall in European power prices that restarts idled capacity, or a stall in Chinese restocking; Alcoa's +5.13% session shows how fast the equity reprices in either direction (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16).
Trigger to Watch

Andy Home noted that even an LME stocks surge failed to cool the market [[n0177]]. A second inventory build that does cool prices would be the exit signal; continued tightness through any Ukraine resolution would confirm the energy-cost floor.

underowned.title: Gold miners: operating leverage over bullion
parts: Attention Gap

Gold has quietly firmed to 1,871.50 USD/oz, +1.90% over five sessions, while GDX gained +6.14% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). Reuters reported gold jumping as rising Ukraine tensions spurred safe-haven demand [[n2192]].
Exposure & Risk

Barrick said it delivered on guidance and opened new exploration frontiers [[n0831]], and Newmont closed at 64.28 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). Miners carry cost inflation and leverage to the gold price in both directions, so a hawkish real-rate move hurts them more than bullion.
Trigger to Watch

Elements by Visual Capitalist explained how interest rate hikes affect gold's price [[n1962]], which frames the test: if gold holds while the 2Y keeps rising from 1.52%, the miner rerating has further to run (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-16).

underowned.title: Nuclear fuel and small reactors
parts: Attention Gap

Nuclear is re-entering European energy policy with little equity follow-through. Forbes reported France vowing to build more nuclear after high gas prices [[n1986]], yet the URA uranium ETF is -4.17% over 20 sessions at 21.62 USD and Cameco -5.49% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16).
Exposure & Risk

Cameco at 21.53 USD and Centrus Energy at 44.46 USD are the listed exposure (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). Reuters reported Macron betting on nuclear and announcing new reactors in a carbon-neutrality push [[n1901]]. The risk is time: reactor programmes take years while the shares trade on uranium sentiment.
Trigger to Watch

Central European orders are the catalyst, with eKoszalin reporting KGHM targeting small modular reactors in Poland by 2029 [[n1776]]. Firm contracts that turn policy into equipment and fuel demand would close the gap.

crypto.title: Bitcoin holds its rebound under a regulatory cloud
parts: Market Context

Bitcoin closed its last completed UTC day at 43,961.86 USD, -1.38% on the day but +18.37% over 20 daily closes, and Ether at 3,127.83 USD, +29.09% over the same span (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-16). Higher beta has led the rebound from late January, with XRP +37.82% over 20 closes at 0.84 USD. Listed proxies have lagged the coins, a sign that equity investors are not chasing: Coinbase Global closed at 207.96 USD, -5.26% over 20 sessions, and MicroStrategy is -5.53% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). CNBC framed the outlook for bitcoin around rising geopolitical tensions and interest rates [[n2203]], the two macro inputs that tie crypto to growth equities.
New / Most Important

The Financial Stability Board warned of emerging risks from crypto-assets to global financial stability [[n1025]], an institutional signal that regulation will tighten as the asset class grows. Politics is noisier: Reuters reported El Salvador's Bukele telling bitcoin-wary US senators to stay out of internal affairs [[n1023]]. Adoption keeps broadening at the edges. Fortune reported Warren Buffett, years after calling bitcoin rat poison, investing $1 billion in a crypto-friendly bank [[n0941]], and Reuters reported Coinbase letting recipients in Mexico cash out in local currency [[n1006]]. Bloomberg said the Super Bowl ad blitz told Americans to stop worrying and buy crypto [[n0637]], but The Seattle Times reported those crypto millions did not drive downloads [[n0113]].
Playbook

Action: hold core bitcoin exposure but do not add through miners or exchange equities until they confirm the coin rebound. Trigger: a daily close back below the 37,138.23 USD level of 20 closes ago would signal a retest of the January low (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-16), while Coinbase back above its 219.50 USD level of 20 sessions ago would confirm equity buyers returning (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). What changes the call: a larger-than-expected Fed step would hit crypto as the longest-duration risk asset.

flows.title: Central banks drain, credit softens, buyers get selective
parts: Global Liquidity

Global liquidity is turning from tailwind to headwind on a staggered schedule. A Reuters commentary argued the historic central-bank drain questions the buy-the-dip reflex [[n1340]], and the Fed's minutes left the pace of tightening open [[n2224]]. The Sydney Morning Herald reported Australia ending QE with a murky future for its asset holdings [[n0023]]. China is the offset, with Bloomberg reporting the PBOC pumping in more liquidity [[n0238]]. The net effect is tighter dollar liquidity alongside looser renminbi liquidity, consistent with Hong Kong outperforming Shanghai and with dollar-denominated emerging-market debt weakening: EMB is -1.17% over 20 sessions at 103.44 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16).
Rates & Dollar

The dollar is not the pressure valve this time. The DXY closed at 95.70 index points, -0.30% on the session and only +0.20% over 20 sessions, while the 2Y rose +48 bps over 20 observations (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16; US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-16). Reuters reported the dollar gaining as Ukraine worries rose and Bullard reiterated his rate comments [[n0114]], but the haven bid has been brief. Treasuries are doing the adjusting: TLT is -3.75% over 20 sessions, IEF -1.54% and even SHY -0.79%. Morningstar asked why inflation-protected bond funds are losing money [[n1353]]; the likely answer is that real yields are rising as nominal yields climb faster than inflation compensation. CNBC reported the 10-year Treasury yield topping 2% for the first time since 2019 after the hot inflation data [[n2175]], and that threshold is now the reference point for every duration-sensitive asset class, from mortgages to growth equities.
Credit Check

Credit is softening at the margin rather than breaking. HYG closed at 83.12 USD, +0.56% on the session but -2.89% over 20 sessions, and LQD is -3.78% over 20 sessions at 123.29 USD, a duration loss more than a default signal (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). Reuters reported global companies slowing debt-raising as yields climb [[n1370]], the first sign of primary-market discipline, while Artemis reported insurance bonds showing resilience as spreads reset [[n1362]]. The stress pocket is Chinese property, where Cedar's failure to pay $3.1 billion overdue [[n0228]] shows the developer chain still defaulting even as Beijing eases. In the US, the warning signs to watch are high-yield outflows and a widening gap between HYG and LQD performance; for now both are losing money mainly through rates.
Equity & Fund Flows

Disclosed positioning points to selective rather than wholesale de-risking. CNBC reported Berkshire increasing an energy bet by more than a third [[n0604]] and buying about $1 billion of Activision shares before Microsoft's deal [[n0577]]. Business Insider reported Stanley Druckenmiller dumping Meta before its $230 billion wipeout [[n0777]], and Reuters reported California and Texas pension funds among new investors in Rivian [[n0677]]. Hedging is active: Bloomberg reported a big options trade hedging an S&P 500 plunge of up to 20% by April [[n2201]]. The Straits Times reported Temasek adding stakes in Grab, Robinhood and other consumer-focused companies [[n1859]]. Primary markets are still open for scale: CNBC reported India's Life Insurance Corporation filing for an $8 billion IPO [[n1355]], and Reuters reported Warburg and Sternlicht SPACs discussing a $20-bln, three-way deal for Allied Universal [[n1359]]. Bloomberg said Cathie Wood's ARKK is a year from its peak and still struggling [[n1865]], and the fund fell -3.20% on the session to 72.87 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16).
Portfolio Implication

The flow evidence supports the macro tilt: keep duration short, own real assets and cash-returning businesses, and fund them from long-duration growth that still depends on cheap money. In practice that means energy and materials over innovation baskets, Hong Kong over onshore China, and short-dated investment grade over high yield until primary issuance reopens; XLE is +6.66% over 20 sessions against ARKK at -3.80% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). The trigger to reverse is a decisive Ukraine de-escalation combined with a 25 bps March signal [[n1360]], which would compress volatility and bring buyers back to growth. The risk is an escalation that lifts the VIX above its 24.29 close and forces correlated selling across all of these positions.

anticipatory.title: Ukraine: pull-back claims against a growing build-up
parts: What Is Priced

Markets are pricing partial de-escalation. CNBC reported Russia saying it had begun a partial troop pullback while NATO urged caution [[n1475]]. The VIX fell -5.49% on the session to 24.29 index points and TTF gas is -6.21% over five sessions at 69.79 EUR/MWh, yet gold is still +1.90% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16).
Conditional Expression

If NATO's view that Russia is increasing troop numbers at the border proves right [[n1498]], the expression is long Brent and gold against European equities, with the Euro Stoxx 50 at 4,137.22 index points already -3.07% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). If the pullback is genuine, the reverse trade is to buy back European banks such as Societe Generale, which is -4.87% over five sessions.
Risk

The Guardian quoted a top NATO official saying Russia is still building forces on the border [[n1502]], and CBS News noted that Russian lawmakers' request for Putin to recognise Ukraine's breakaway regions gives him another card to play [[n1503]]. A recognition move would be the fastest route from relief to a sanctions shock.

anticipatory.title: March FOMC: 25 or 50
parts: What Is Priced

The 2Y at 1.52%, after rising +48 bps over 20 observations, prices a March lift-off with fast follow-through (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-16). Reuters reported hot inflation fuelling the case for a big-bang rate hike in March [[n2184]], while Richmond Fed President Barkin said he would have to be convinced of the need for a half-point move [[n1342]].
Conditional Expression

If inflation data or Fed speakers push the market toward a half-point step, extend the 2s10s flattener and favour bank equities over long-duration software. If officials lean toward a quarter point, which the minutes' flexibility allows [[n1369]], the 2Y has room to stabilise and punished growth can bounce; ARKK is -3.80% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16).
Risk

Bloomberg's warning that Treasury market liquidity is eroding [[n2215]] means either outcome could move yields further than fundamentals justify. A disorderly long-end selloff that steepens the curve would hurt banks and growth at the same time. A Board still waiting on confirmation of nominees such as Sarah Bloom Raskin [[n2214]] adds uncertainty about how hawkish the voting mix will be.

anticipatory.title: Iran deal: removing the oil risk premium
parts: What Is Priced

Brent at 94.81 USD/bbl and WTI at 93.66 USD/bbl price a tight market carrying a war premium (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). Reuters reported the State Department saying the US is in the very final stages of Iran nuclear talks [[n1506]], after Reuters had reported Iran's oil exports rising as talks resumed [[n1377]].
Conditional Expression

A signed deal would add Iranian barrels to an already rising flow; the expression is to fade front-month crude against later-dated contracts and rotate from pure crude producers toward gas-levered ones. Without a deal, the tighter balance confirmed by the IEA's demand revision [[n0641]] keeps the premium, and energy stays the portfolio hedge, especially as The Intercept reported Saudi Arabia rejecting Biden's plea to raise production [[n1990]].
Risk

Talks have stalled before: The Guardian reported them stalling as Tehran urged the US to accept its terms [[n1447]], and Al Jazeera reported Iran saying the outcome hinges on Western decisions [[n1448]]. A collapse alongside a Ukraine escalation would push crude beyond the 7-year highs Reuters reported [[n0120]].

anticipatory.title: China easing against Fed tightening
parts: What Is Priced

Hong Kong is pricing easing and the mainland is not yet. The Hang Seng is +1.38% over 20 sessions while the Shanghai Composite is -3.66%, and FXI is +0.63% over 20 sessions at 38.10 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). Reuters reported slowing inflation leaving room for policy easing [[n0245]], and CNBC reported investment banks saying it is time to buy Chinese stocks [[n0247]].
Conditional Expression

If the PBOC follows the January reductions that the BBC reported as China cutting interest rates while growth slowed [[n0150]], the expression is long China internet through KWEB against US software, a direct bet on policy divergence. If policy stays on hold, prefer Chinese banks and infrastructure to consumer names.
Risk

A weaker yuan is the side effect, with Reuters linking its slip to divergent China-U.S. monetary policy [[n0254]]; a disorderly move could trigger outflows. US trade pressure is the second risk, after the BBC reported Washington accusing China of serious harm through trade [[n0274]].

catalysts.title: Nvidia (NVDA)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Al Jazeera reported Nvidia forecasting upbeat current-quarter revenue [[n2006]] alongside its fourth-quarter and fiscal 2022 results [[n0140]]. The thesis is data-centre and gaming demand strong enough to carry a premium multiple through a rate shock.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The pre-results close was 265.11 USD, +5.76% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). Techcircle reported the FTC saying the termination of Nvidia's attempt to buy Arm bodes well for competition [[n2018]]; the lost deal removes an option, not the core business. The risk is guidance that only meets a very high bar.
Trade Expression
Hold rather than chase. Add on a pullback toward the 250.67 USD level of 20 sessions ago if guidance holds, and hedge with SOXX while yields keep rising.

catalysts.title: Cisco Systems (CSCO)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Reuters reported Cisco raising its annual earnings forecast and announcing $15 billion in buybacks [[n1181]]. The thesis is supply finally converting backlog into revenue plus heavy cash returns; the WSJ had reported a $20 billion-plus takeover offer for Splunk [[n1094]], a sign management wants software growth.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The pre-results close was 54.25 USD, -7.89% over 20 sessions and below the 58.90 USD of 20 sessions ago (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). The risk is that a large software deal dilutes the buyback story.
Trade Expression
Buy on confirmation that the post-results gain holds, targeting a retest of 58.90 USD; cut if the shares slip back below 54.25 USD, which would mean the market doubts the raised forecast.

catalysts.title: DoorDash (DASH)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

PYMNTS reported DoorDash at 25M active users and eyeing category expansion [[n1184]]. The thesis is that delivery has become habit rather than a lockdown artefact, with rising fee power: the WSJ reported DoorDash raising fees for McDonald's restaurants that keep drivers waiting [[n0590]].
Price Hurdle & Risk

The regular session closed at 94.89 USD, -6.80% before the report and -27.98% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16), so the after-hours jump starts from a depressed base. The risk is that reopening shifts spending back to restaurants' own channels.
Trade Expression
Buy only if the shares hold the post-results gap over the following sessions; the first upside hurdle is the 131.76 USD level of 20 sessions ago. A close back below 94.89 USD would void the setup.

catalysts.title: Airbnb (ABNB)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

CNBC reported Airbnb beating on earnings with strong guidance [[n0660]], and its CFO told Marketing Week the company was right to shift spending from performance marketing to brand-building [[n0826]], which supports margins as travel reopens.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The shares closed at 186.64 USD, +3.65% on the session and +20.74% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). The risk is tighter regulation of short-term rentals; Airbnb said it supports registration across G4 cities [[n1180]].
Trade Expression

Hold core exposure and add on dips toward the 154.58 USD level of 20 sessions ago, pairing it against lockdown winners such as Peloton. The call changes if guidance on the travel recovery is cut or a new variant closes borders again.

catalysts.title: Shopify (SHOP)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Al Jazeera reported Shopify plunging on a weaker growth outlook [[n2015]], following its fourth-quarter and full-year 2021 results [[n1203]]. Business Insider reported analysts naming Amazon, Lightspeed and BigCommerce as Shopify's biggest worries [[n1121]]. The thesis is slower merchant growth meeting heavier investment.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The stock closed at 746.85 USD, -16.04% on the session and -27.56% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). The risk to a bearish view is a sharp short-covering bounce if yields ease.
Trade Expression

Sell rallies that fail to recover a meaningful part of the -19.26% five-session loss, or pair a short against Amazon at 3,162.01 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16). The call changes if merchant growth reaccelerates in the next quarter.

catalysts.title: Intel (INTC)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Bloomberg reported Intel's CEO is tired of Wall Street doubting his comeback plan [[n1192]], and Al Jazeera reported Intel buying Israel's Tower Semiconductor in a $5.4BN deal [[n1987]]. The thesis is a foundry pivot that needs time and capital.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The stock closed at 48.23 USD, -10.05% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-16), and Notebookcheck reported AMD overtaking Intel's market cap for the first time after the Xilinx merger [[n0823]]. The risk is that capital spending rises before revenue does.
Trade Expression
Stay neutral. A credible margin path at the next strategy update would justify buying toward the 53.62 USD level of 20 sessions ago, while another guidance cut would confirm share loss.
